problem: Netflix wanted its streaming and DVD businesses to evolve independently.
title: Netflix plans to split DVD and streaming into Qwikster, then cancels
context: In 2011 Netflix raised prices and announced that its DVD-by-mail service would be separated from streaming under the name Qwikster.
decision_made: Split DVD rental into a separate brand and website, Qwikster, with separate accounts.
action_taken: CEO Reed Hastings posted an apology but kept the plan; about three weeks later Netflix dropped Qwikster and kept one site and one account.
observed_outcome: The split was cancelled on 10 Oct 2011 and the price increase stayed. Reports say Netflix lost subscribers in Q3 2011; estimates differ by source.
observation_period: About 3 weeks from announcement to reversal
lessons: Customer-facing changes that add friction (two sites, two accounts) can be reversed quickly if the backlash is strong, even when the underlying strategy is unchanged.
limitations: Subscriber-loss figures vary between sources (about 800,000 vs about 2 million). The price increase and the split were combined, so their effects cannot be separated.

claims.claim_text: Netflix planned to split its DVD service into a separate Qwikster brand alongside a price increase.
Netflix dropped Qwikster and kept DVDs and streaming under one site and account, while the price increase remained.
